runs_no_backtest: this job re-computes nothing. It applies TRIAL-DRAFT-B §5 to numbers a named receipt already carries, so its output can be checked against that receipt by hand.
decision_rule: TRIAL-DRAFT-B §5. FAILED_VARIANT if the net block-mean is <= 0, OR the same-day arm outperforms non-cluster purchases, OR post-floor attrition leaves < 10 names/year. PRODUCT_PROMISING needs the block-mean >= the computed MDE of 7.17% at t >= 2.0 with the falsifier surviving and >= 20 names/year. Everything between is CONDITIONAL.
power_finding: §4, computed BEFORE the read: the MDE is 0.0717 per block against a published gap of 0.05, so this design cannot confirm its own prior at 80% power. That changes what the trial may CONCLUDE, not whether it runs — and its protection is explicitly conditional on the point estimate being above zero.

falsifier_status.why: the same-day arm reads -0.00325 on 2017-2024 and -0.001574 pooled against its random Form-4-active twin. §5's clause 2 fires only if it OUTPERFORMS; it does not, so the mechanism's falsifier SURVIVES — which closes nothing and rescues nothing. A falsifier that passes is not evidence for the book.

numbers.power_warning: the registered MDE (7.17%) is ABOVE the published effect (5.0%): a non-significant result here is CONDITIONAL, never FAILED_VARIANT, unless the point estimate is <= 0

tradability_clause.why: run 1's receipt carries no post-floor name count per year, so §5's '< 10 names/year' clause has no input. A guard DERIVES its inputs or REFUSES; treating an unmeasured clause as passed is how a gate stops being read. The cluster panel's own per-year count is what would answer it.

next_test: MORE BLOCKS, i.e. time, is the only honest route to power on this construction (§4.3) — and a wider event definition is a NEW REGISTRATION, not an amendment.
